display.purpose: Page titles. One per route, solid ink, never gradient-filled.

headline.purpose: Section titles inside the lattice, always paired with a bottom rule.

body.purpose: Ledes and section copy in the site chrome, held to 65 to 75 characters.

prose.purpose: The 15px long-form reading size at 1.75 leading, for governance documents and work write-ups.

supporting.purpose: Captions, cell descriptions, navigation, and inline links. The Geist Sans floor of the ramp.

readout.purpose: Statistics and headline numbers in Geist Mono with tabular figures.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, dates, identifiers, and stack tags. The panel's engraving.

meta.purpose: The monospaced value under an engraved label; also figure captions and document tables.

motion.name: ease-instrument
motion.purpose: The system's only easing curve, expo-out. New motion changes duration, not curve.

motion.name: duration-entrance
motion.purpose: BlurFade default entrance for heroes and figures.

motion.name: duration-sweep
motion.purpose: RevealLine hairline sweep under a section header, drawn in ink rather than blue.

motion.name: duration-hero-rules
motion.purpose: HeroRules settling from scaleX 1.06 to 1 with opacity on mount.

motion.name: duration-count
motion.purpose: Statistic count-up, decoration over an already-correct value.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Colour and background state transitions on rows, links, and controls.

motion.name: duration-chrome
motion.purpose: Header transition between transparent and blurred states.

motion.name: duration-theme
motion.purpose: Theme toggle, the one ease-out exception to the single-curve rule.

motion.name: spring-nav
motion.purpose: Active navigation underline travelling between routes. Collapses to zero duration under reduced motion.

motion.name: marquee
motion.purpose: Partner strip translation. Disabled entirely under reduced motion.

narrative.overview:
LinkScape reads as precision hardware rather than a student club. The visitor is a sixteen-year-old deciding whether these people are serious, and the interface answers before the copy does: everything is aligned to a rule, every number is monospaced and right-weighted, contrast is high, and nothing is decorated for the sake of looking designed. The feeling to aim for is a well-built measuring device. It is legible at a glance, it tells you exactly one thing per readout, and its restraint is what makes it credible.

The system is built from rules and cells, never from floating cards. Content sits inside a bordered lattice that runs the full width of the page, and the hero opens with vertical hairlines pitched to the exact column count of the band beneath it, so the ruling the visitor meets at the top of the page is literally the ruling that carries the content. Surfaces are flat without exception: depth is a one-pixel rule and a one-step tonal lift, and there is no shadow anywhere in the page body. Where a diagram, figure, or number can carry the point, it replaces the paragraph.

Color is nearly absent by design. Ink on paper does the work, and a single GitHub-derived blue marks the things a visitor can act on. Three treatments are explicitly rejected: gradient-filled headings, any decorative background field that is not structurally connected to the page grid, and any atmospheric glow laid behind content. All three were present in an earlier build, all three are recognizable signatures of machine-generated interfaces, and this organization is judged on the appearance of being genuinely built.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled cells, not cards. The border is the container.
Flat everywhere. No shadow carries structure, state, or atmosphere.
Monospace for every number, identifier, and label.
One accent color, reserved for action.
Both themes are authored, neither is derived.
The page must be readable and navigable with JavaScript disabled.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the system's only chromatic color, and it means "you can act on this." A chip, a tag, a category, or a heading never earns color. If something needs to be distinguished and it is not actionable, distinguish it with a rule, a monospace label, or position.

rules.name: The Two Value Rule
rules.body: Light and dark are separately authored, not algorithmically inverted. Every new color must be specified in both, and a design is not finished until it has been read in both.

rules.name: The Rule Carries Structure
rules.body: Before reaching for a background, a shadow, or a radius to separate two things, use a one-pixel border in Rule. That is the house style and it is almost always sufficient.

rules.name: The Stencil Is Not A Color Rule
rules.body: A value that exists only to make a mask opaque does not enter the palette, does not get a dark variant, and does not get reused as a fill. If it ever paints a pixel the visitor can see, it has become a color and must be justified as one.

rules.name: The Engraved Label Rule
rules.body: Anything that names, dates, categorizes, or identifies is set in Geist Mono, uppercase, at 11px with 0.14em tracking. Anything that argues or explains is set in Geist Sans. A visitor can tell fact from framing by typeface alone.

rules.name: The Measured Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: An eyebrow carries a count, a date, a status, or an identifier: "12 projects", "Founded 2023", "4 published · 11 registered". It never paraphrases the heading beneath it. If the only eyebrow you can write restates the section title, delete it. The engraved label is instrumentation, and a decorative caption set in that typeface turns the whole panel into a costume.

rules.name: The Solid Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings are one solid color. No gradient fill, no background-clip: text, no per-word tinting. A heading that needs a gradient to be interesting is a heading with nothing to say.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: Every figure a reader might compare or scan is monospaced with tabular figures. Numbers in running prose are exempt.

rules.name: The Continuous Rule Rule
rules.body: The two vertical container borders never break between sections. If a new section cannot draw them, it belongs inside an existing one.

rules.name: The Flush Grid Rule
rules.body: Grid cells clip their trailing borders against an overflow-hidden parent. Never hand-remove borders from the last item in a row; the column count changes at every breakpoint and the hand-removal will be wrong.

rules.name: The Matched Pitch Rule
rules.body: Any full-bleed ruling laid behind content is inset to the container's own gutters and pitched to the column count of the band directly below it, so its lines fall on real cell divisions. A field that does not land on the grid is decoration, and decoration behind content is the thing this system exists to refuse.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest, flat on hover, and flat on press. There are no permitted shadows in the page body: not on a button, not on a card, not on a cell, not on a chip, not on a hero. A new box-shadow is a defect, and the correct fix is a rule or a tonal step.

rules.name: The No Atmosphere Rule
rules.body: Depth is never suggested by light. No radial glow, no bloom, no vignette, no gradient fading into the page floor. If a region needs to feel separate, give it a border and a surface value.

rules.name: The Two File Figure Rule
rules.body: Any generated graphic ships as a light and a dark variant. A single graphic that "works on both" is a graphic that is wrong on one.

rules.name: The No Placeholder Number Rule
rules.body: An unsubstantiated figure is stated as absent in words. It is never zero, never an approximation, and never a dash.

rules.name: The One Ease Rule
rules.body: Every transition in the system uses expo-out cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1). New motion changes duration, not curve.

rules.name: The Reading Is Not An Entrance Rule
rules.body: Continuous prose is never staggered. Animate the frame, the figure, and the rule; never the sentence the reader is trying to get to.

rules.name: The Category Mark Rule
rules.body: Category is the one other thing permitted colour, and it wears it as a 6px mark beside a word that already says the same thing. Three marks exist and they are never recycled for a fourth meaning. Text stays ink, so contrast never depends on the mark.

rules.name: The Validated Set Rule
rules.body: The category marks were checked as a categorical palette in both themes against the real surface. Software and Event separate by deltaE 6.9 under deuteranopia in light and 7.1 in dark, in the floor band, which is legal only because every mark ships beside its own word. To normal vision the same pair separates by 23.8 and 25.1. Change a mark and the set is re-validated.

dos: Do separate content with a one-pixel solid border in Rule before considering a background, radius, or shadow.
Do set every number, identifier, date, label, and stack tag in Geist Mono, and use tabular figures wherever numbers can be compared.
Do write eyebrows as measured keys: a count, a date, a status, an identifier.
Do author both themes explicitly, and read every new surface in both before calling it done.
Do keep the two vertical container rules unbroken from the header to the footer.
Do inset any full-bleed ruling to the container gutters and pitch it onto the lattice's cell divisions.
Do initialize animated values at their true state so the page is correct with JavaScript disabled, and let animation affect timing only, never the rendered tree.
Do let a figure, a readout, or a table replace a paragraph when it can carry the same meaning.
Do reserve Signal Blue for things the visitor can act on.
donts: Don't apply a gradient to text, ever. No background-clip: text, no tinted headings.
Don't add a decorative background field that is unconnected to the page grid. Hero background structure must be an extension of the lattice, not a tiled pattern laid behind it.
Don't introduce a box-shadow. The system has none and needs none.
Don't add a glow, bloom, vignette, or radial atmosphere to suggest depth.
Don't use a dashed border. Every rule in the system is solid.
Don't tint chip text or fill a chip with a hue. A category wears its color as the 6px mark and states itself in words; default is neutral and strong is status.
Don't round anything embedded in the lattice. Squares meet; pills float.
Don't add a type size between the nine ramp steps.
Don't write an eyebrow that restates the heading below it. Delete it instead.
Don't stagger paragraphs of continuous prose.
Don't invent a metric, a placeholder number, or a rounded estimate. If the figure is not substantiated, the design must hold with it absent.
Don't use an em dash in interface copy, and don't define anything by what it is not.
Don't branch the rendered markup on reduced motion. Change the transition, not the tree, or server and client will disagree and content will strand invisible.
Don't put category colour on text, and don't add a fourth category mark without re-running the palette validation.

typographyMeta.fine: The footnote tier at 12px. Statistic notes, disclaimer bands, chip and small-button text, register table cells, and the footer legal line. It never carries an argument, only a qualification on something stated above it.
